questions.question: What is the Gracie Barra motto?
questions.explanation: Gracie Barra's motto is 'Jiu-Jitsu for Everyone!' — it means BJJ is for all kids, families, and people everywhere.

questions.question: What do GB students say when they greet their professor?
questions.explanation: 'Oss!' is the special Gracie Barra greeting — it means 'I respect you and I'm ready to learn!'

questions.question: What colour is the Gracie Barra logo?
questions.explanation: The GB logo is red and white — you'll see it on your gi patch and on the school walls!

questions.question: What do we call the uniform you wear in Jiu-Jitsu class?
questions.explanation: The 'Gi' (or 'Kimono') is the special jacket and pants you wear in BJJ — it has lots of grips for techniques!

questions.question: What is the mat area in a Jiu-Jitsu school called?
questions.explanation: The mat area is called the 'Tatami' — it's the soft mat that keeps you safe when you train!

questions.question: Before you step on the mat, what should you always do?
answers: Bow or say Oss as a sign of respect
questions.explanation: Bowing or saying 'Oss' before stepping on the mat shows respect for the school and your training partners.

questions.question: What is your teacher called at Gracie Barra?
questions.explanation: At GB, instructors are called 'Professor' — it's a sign of respect for all they have learned and teach.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep your gi clean?
answers: Respect for yourself and your training partners — hygiene is part of the code
questions.explanation: A clean gi shows respect for your training partners and the school. It's part of the Gracie Barra code!

questions.question: What is the very first belt every new student gets?
questions.explanation: White belt is where everyone starts — even the best black belts in the world began as white belts!

questions.question: In the kids program, what belt comes after white?
questions.explanation: Kids belts go through yellow and grey before reaching the higher colours — each one means you've learned new skills!

questions.question: How do you earn a stripe on your belt?
answers: Training hard, learning techniques, and showing respect
questions.explanation: Stripes come from working hard, attending class, learning new techniques, and being a good training partner!

questions.question: How many stripes can you get before moving to the next belt?
questions.explanation: You can earn up to 4 stripes on each belt. After 4 stripes, you might be ready for the next belt colour!

questions.question: What does it mean when someone has a black belt?
answers: They have trained for many years and mastered the basics
They are the youngest in the school
questions.explanation: Black belt means many years of hard training, dedication, and mastery — it's a huge achievement!

questions.question: Should you be upset if someone else gets their belt before you?
answers: Yes, it means you are bad
No — everyone learns at their own pace. Focus on your own progress!
Yes, train less until they catch up
questions.explanation: Everyone learns differently! Focus on your own journey — your time will come if you keep training!

questions.question: What colour belt do you get in the kids program after green?
questions.explanation: In the GB kids system, after green comes blue — which is also the first adult belt! Big milestone!

questions.question: Why does your professor tie your belt at promotion?
answers: As a sign of respect and to officially welcome you to the new rank
Because you can't tie it yourself
So it stays tight during sparring
questions.explanation: When your professor ties your belt at promotion, it's a special moment of respect — they're welcoming you to your new rank!

questions.question: What do you do when you want the sparring to stop?
questions.explanation: Tapping 3 times (or saying 'tap!') is the signal to stop — your partner MUST let go immediately. It keeps everyone safe!

questions.question: Why is it important to tap when you're in a tough spot?
answers: It keeps you safe so you can train again tomorrow!
It means you have to leave class
Professor gets angry if you don't
questions.explanation: Tapping is smart, not weak! It means 'I'll try again' — staying safe means you can keep training!

questions.question: What is a 'sweep' in BJJ?
answers: Cleaning the mat with a broom
Rolling your partner so they go to the bottom and you're on top
questions.explanation: A sweep flips the positions — you go from being on bottom to being on top! It's like reversing the game.

questions.question: What is a 'shrimp move' used for in BJJ?
answers: Moving your hips away to create space and escape
questions.explanation: Shrimping (hip escape) helps you create space to get your legs free — like a little shrimp wiggling away!

questions.question: What does 'guard' mean in Jiu-Jitsu?
answers: A security guard at the door
Using your legs to control or stop your opponent while on your back
questions.explanation: Guard is when you use your legs to control your opponent from your back — your legs are your tools!

questions.question: What is a 'takedown'?
answers: Taking your partner from standing to the ground
Pulling down on the gi collar
questions.explanation: A takedown moves the fight from standing to the ground — where BJJ really shines!

questions.question: Why is Jiu-Jitsu called the 'Gentle Art'?
answers: Because it uses leverage and technique, not just strength
Because you wear soft gi fabric
questions.explanation: BJJ is called the Gentle Art because a smaller person can use technique and leverage to overcome a bigger, stronger opponent!

questions.question: What technique is like a tight hug around someone's waist from behind?
questions.explanation: A body lock or back clinch wraps your arms around your opponent's waist from behind — great control!

questions.question: What is the 'Mount' position?
answers: Sitting on top of your partner's chest/stomach
questions.explanation: Mount means you're sitting on top of your partner — it's one of the strongest positions in BJJ!

questions.question: When someone is in your 'Closed Guard', where are your legs?
answers: Crossed and locked around your partner's waist
questions.explanation: Closed guard = your legs locked around your partner's waist. You're on your back but still in control!

questions.question: What is 'Side Control'?
answers: Lying sideways across your partner's body while on top
questions.explanation: Side Control means you're lying across your partner from the side — you're on top but sideways! It's very strong.

questions.question: If you're on your partner's back with your legs hooked in, what position is that?
questions.explanation: Back Control means you're behind your partner with your legs hooked in — like a human backpack! Very strong position.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'pass the guard'?
answers: Getting past your partner's legs to a better position on top
questions.explanation: Passing the guard means getting through your partner's legs so you can get on top in a better position!

questions.question: What position are you in when you're on your back with your partner kneeling between your legs?
answers: Guard (your partner is in your guard!)
questions.explanation: When your partner is kneeling between your legs and you're on your back, they're inside your Guard — you can attack from here!

questions.question: Why do you want to be on top in BJJ?
answers: Top positions give you more control and options to attack
questions.explanation: Being on top gives you control and gravity on your side — it's harder for your partner to attack you from the bottom!

questions.question: What is the 'Turtle' position?
answers: Curling up on all fours to protect yourself like a turtle shell
questions.explanation: Turtling means you curl up on hands and knees to protect your neck — just like a turtle hiding in its shell!

questions.question: Jiu-Jitsu originally came from which country?
questions.explanation: Jiu-Jitsu started in Japan a long, long time ago — then it travelled to Brazil where the Gracie family made it famous!

questions.question: Who is the founder of Gracie Barra?
questions.explanation: Carlos Gracie Jr. founded Gracie Barra in 1986 in Brazil — and now there are GB schools all over the world including right here!

questions.question: What country did the Gracie family bring Jiu-Jitsu to from Japan?
questions.explanation: A Japanese Judo master named Maeda taught the Gracie family in Brazil — and they turned it into Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu!

questions.question: What does 'BJJ' stand for?
questions.explanation: BJJ = Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu — the art you practice every time you step on the mat at GB Lake Country!

questions.question: Gracie Barra schools can be found in how many countries?
questions.explanation: Gracie Barra has schools in over 50 countries! When you wear your GB gi, you're connected to students all around the world.

questions.question: Why is Jiu-Jitsu called 'the great equalizer'?
answers: Because everyone wears the same gi
Because a smaller person can use technique to beat a bigger, stronger person
Because everyone gets the same belt
Because all classes are the same length
questions.explanation: Jiu-Jitsu is the great equalizer because smart technique beats size and strength — that's why everyone can do it!

questions.question: Gracie Barra Lake Country is in which province of Canada?
questions.explanation: GB Lake Country is in beautiful British Columbia — right in the Okanagan Valley!

questions.question: What is the main thing you learn in Jiu-Jitsu besides techniques?
answers: Respect, discipline, confidence, and never giving up
How to be the loudest in class
How to wear the gi fastest
questions.explanation: BJJ teaches much more than moves — respect, discipline, confidence and perseverance are the real gifts of the gentle art!
